intro.title: INTRODUCTION
intro.problemBody: Online compilers and javac alone give only output or errors. Students never see how Java code becomes tokens, trees, symbol tables, or bytecode.

basics.whatBody: A translator: it converts human-readable source code into machine-executable form before the program runs.
basics.whyBody: Speed (runs natively), portability (write once, run anywhere), safety (errors caught before running).
basics.vsBody: Java compiles first, then runs. JavaScript runs line by line, JIT-ing hot code.

intro.fixBody: Write Java in the Monaco editor in your browser, click Compile, and explore every phase — lexing, parsing, AST, semantic analysis, CFG/optimizer, codegen, bytecode, execution — with interactive D3 and 3D views in English or Myanmar.

objectives.title: OBJECTIVE
objectives.kicker: // 05 — WHAT WE SET OUT TO DO
items: Make every Java compile phase visible step by step (lexing → execution) instead of output-only.
Teach front end / optimizer / back end structure using real, runnable Java code.
Label every visualization with the algorithm that built it (e.g. Maximal-Munch, Shift-Reduce, Graph Coloring).
Let users compile once and explore anywhere across all visualize panels.
Support learning in both English and Myanmar (full i18n).
Provide interactive D3.js views (tokens, AST, symbol table, CFG) plus a 3D pipeline overview.
Enable authenticated saved-code snippets so students revisit examples anytime (JWT + database).
Make the compiling techniques course easy to understand with this project.

er.title: ER DIAGRAM

limitations.title: LIMITATION
items: Error messages are raw javac output

conclusion.title: CONCLUSION
conclusion.body: Compiler Visualizer turns a black-box javac run into an explorable pipeline: one Java file in, tokens, AST, symbol table, optimizer graphs, and bytecode out — each view labeled with its algorithm and explorable in English or Myanmar. It proves the full front end to back end flow works end to end, from editor to execution.
